newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian rouble, T-bills edge down on roubles galore.
newsitem.headline: Russian rouble, T-bills edge down on roubles galore.

text.p: A rouble surplus after Wednesday's T-bill auctions pushed down GKO Treasury bills yields and rouble rates on the interbank market on Thursday, dealers said.
They forecast a further downward trend in the next few days with the exception of some undervalued OFZ interest-bearing bonds.
Renaissance capital chief analyst Roland Nash said yields had fallen by an average 25 basis points, with the yield on a one-year T-bill falling to 18.60 from 18.84 percent.
*Turnover rose to 4.34 trln rbls from 3.55 trln rbls on Tuesday
*Central bank sold 579 bln rbls of bills and bonds

"It is no wonder that the yields have fallen, as there was a lot of money left after the auctions -- 2.5 or 3.0 trillion roubles -- and since interbank roubles are cheap, all T-bills rose," said Alfa-Bank dealer Dmitry Ivanov.
Banks bid a total of 11.57 trillion roubles at yesterday's auctions, while the Finance Ministry only sold 8.11 trillion roubles of paper.
Dealers said the rouble could have depreciated further but had run up against the lower limit of the central bank's daily bid/offer rates.
Higher yields obtainable on overnight dollar credits compared with rouble credits was also fuelling demand for dollars.
